dedupe_keys.name: influence of epistemic and aleatory modeling uncertainty on the seismic collapse capacity of reinforced concrete components

description: Influence of Epistemic and Aleatory Modeling Uncertainty on the Seismic Collapse Capacity of Reinforced Concrete Components is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "simulation", published or maintained by Maha Kenawy, Oklahoma State University (okstate.edu). Assessment of extreme limit states in structures due to earthquake loading may be associated with significant uncertainty due to the randomness in structural and material properties (aleatory uncertainty), and the bias induced by numerical simulation of the strength and stiffness deterioration mechanisms (epistemic uncertainty). Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "simulation" project. Keywords: modeling uncertainty, seismic collapse assessment, aftershock collapse fragility, post-peak structural behavior. Published 2026-01-19. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
